extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funding (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, and institutional legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing and complying with 34 C.F.R. §106.44's duties for Title IX Coordinators and recipients to monitor for barriers to reporting sex discrimination and to satisfy employee notification requirements. Includes what must be monitored, who must notify, limits (confidentiality/First Amendment), and acceptable remedial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring for barriers to reporting (§106.44(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must monitor the recipient's education program or activity for barriers to reporting information about conduct that 'reasonably' may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department interprets this as a specific duty to monitor for barriers to reporting (not to monitor all conduct). Monitoring may include assessing access to reporting systems, campus climate indicators, staff feedback, focus groups, or surveys. The final text specifies monitoring 'for barriers to reporting information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to take steps reasonably calculated to address identified barriers (§106.44(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient (through its Title IX Coordinator) becomes aware of a barrier to reporting sex discrimination, the recipient must take steps that are reasonably calculated to address that barrier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses should be tailored to the specific impediments and obstacles identified. Examples include targeted trainings, more prominent publication of Title IX Coordinator contact information, relocating the Coordinator's office for visibility/accessibility, providing adequate staff, enhancing employee training to avoid conflicts of interest or discouragement of reporting, and developing user-friendly Title IX materials. The obligation is ongoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailoring responses to local circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's response to identified reporting barriers should be tailored to the specific impediments and the characteristics of the recipient's educational environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have flexibility to choose strategies appropriate to size, resources, and administrative structure. Possible actions include department-specific trainings, student surveys or focus groups to understand discouragement or fear of retaliation, or institution-wide communications emphasizing non-retaliation. The Department declines to mandate particular monitoring tools (e.g., campus surveys).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on monitoring — scope and First Amendment/academic freedom protections
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(b) does not require monitoring of all conduct, students' online activity, or classroom academic discourse; Title IX must be interpreted consistently with First Amendment protections and academic freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not expected to monitor students' social media or classroom speech. If speech (including protected speech) creates a barrier to reporting, recipients must address barriers in ways that do not infringe protected rights — for example, by clarifying reporting policies rather than policing viewpoint-based speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of confidential resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not compromise confidential resources to monitor for barriers to reporting; confidential employees remain able to provide support without being forced to report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If confidential employees mistakenly discourage reporting (e.g., by believing certain conduct need not be reported), the Title IX Coordinator must address such barriers through corrected publicity and training. The final regs preserve the availability of confidential employees who do not have notification requirements (§106.44(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee notification requirements (general) (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must require employees (other than confidential employees) to notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that 'reasonably' may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or, as applicable, provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and information about how to make a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department streamlined and clarified notification requirements and divided §106.44(c) into subsections for different employee categories. The purpose is to ensure the Title IX Coordinator learns of possible sex discrimination so the recipient can act. Employees need not determine definitively that sex discrimination occurred — notification is triggered by information that could reasonably be understood to constitute sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification specifics for elementary and secondary school employees
rubrics_metrics.description: At elementary and secondary schools, all non-confidential employees must notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is broader than the postsecondary framework to reduce burdens on students; non-confidential K-12 employees must notify the Title IX Coordinator rather than merely providing contact information in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification specifics for postsecondary employees
rubrics_metrics.description: At postsecondary institutions, when a student provides information to a non-confidential employee, the employee must either notify the Title IX Coordinator or, as applicable, provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and information about how to make a complaint of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients (other than K-12) have discretion to determine which employees who lack authority to institute corrective action must notify versus merely provide contact info; the Department declined to give broader discretion to narrow notification duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reportable conduct standard — 'reasonably' may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require notification and monitoring for conduct that 'reasonably' may constitute sex discrimination, rather than conduct that 'may' constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that employees should act on information that could reasonably be understood to fall within Title IX's definitions (including sex-based harassment). Employees are not expected to apply the full legal definition in the first instance; observation or receipt of information that could reasonably meet the definition is sufficient to trigger notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirement on scope of sex discrimination (§106.8(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must train all employees on the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination under Title IX, including sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This training helps ensure employees can recognize when information they receive reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and therefore triggers the notification obligation under §106.44(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee duty to explain limits of confidentiality (§106.44(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee must explain to any person who informs them of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination the circumstances in which the employee is not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department modified §106.44(d)(2) to require confidential employees to inform reporters about when confidentiality applies and when they would have notification obligations, preserving complainant autonomy and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and nondisclosure limits (§106.44(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are prohibited from disclosing personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with this part, except in limited circumstances (e.g., to a parent/guardian or authorized legal representative with the legal right to receive disclosures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision addresses concerns that notification requirements could lead to harmful disclosures (e.g., of LGBTQI+ identity or pregnancy information). Recipients must follow §106.44(j) limitations when handling reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient accountability and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The compliance obligation to ensure monitoring and notification falls on the recipient; if a recipient fails to ensure its Title IX Coordinator complies with duties under §106.44(b) (or related provisions), the recipient may be subject to administrative enforcement action and must be provided notice and an opportunity to come into compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Title IX Coordinator may delegate duties to designees, one Title IX Coordinator must retain ultimate oversight (§106.8(a)(2)). Delegation does not relieve the recipient of responsibility. The Department will offer technical assistance and may enforce the requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on evasion via external third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not avoid compliance with §106.44(c) by requiring reporting to an external third party; the recipient must still ensure the report reaches the Title IX Coordinator and maintain oversight if duties are delegated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reporting is routed to an external entity, the Title IX Coordinator must exercise oversight to ensure consistent compliance with Title IX obligations. Recipients cannot use external reporting as a substitute for required notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility and non-mandate of specific monitoring tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to mandate specific steps (e.g., campus surveys) to monitor for barriers to reporting; recipients have flexibility to choose effective strategies suited to their environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Department recognizes campus or climate surveys as useful (and some States/VAWA require them), it will not require particular monitoring practices. Recipients may nonetheless use surveys, focus groups, or other tools if appropriate.
